setup: Forearms on a bench or your thighs
Palms up, wrists just past the edge
execution: Let the bar lower, wrists bending back
Keep a firm hold of the bar
Curl your wrists up as high as they go
Forearms stay flat on the support
faults: Don't lift your forearms to help

notes: Use a light bar and higher reps; small wrist muscles do the work.
Keep the bar under control at the bottom; letting it roll far down the fingers is optional and needs a secure grip.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Close side view at bench height, figure kneeling or seated with forearms along a flat bench, hands just past the edge on the right. Hands and forearms fill most of the frame.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Forearms flat along the bench, palms up, wrists over the edge. Wrists bent back so the bar hangs below the bench top, fingers still closed round the bar.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Wrists curled up as far as they go, bar raised above the bench top. Forearms still flat on the bench.

ikHints: Only the wrists and hands move
guideBrief.barPath: A short arc around the wrists
emphasise: Full range from bent back to curled up
doNotShow: Bar dropping out of the fingers

uncertain.note: StrengthLog lets the bar roll down the fingers; ACE says keep it in the palm. Keeping a firm grip is the default here.
Barbell is the default because it logs one unambiguous total. The dumbbell version (per hand, one or both arms) is listed as a variation with no entry yet.
